p: Shoreditch is packed with things to do before or after your darts session. Boxpark Shoreditch, the pop-up mall built from shipping containers, is a fun spot for street food and independent shops. The Museum of the Home on Kingsland Road, set in beautiful old almshouses, takes you through how people have lived at home over the last 400 years, with period rooms and a lovely garden. And the Barbican, a short walk west, is a brutalist landmark with an arts centre, cinema and a hidden conservatory full of tropical plants.
Hoxton Square, just off Old Street, has been a hub for creative types for years, with bars and restaurants around its central garden. It's a handy spot to start or finish an evening.

For your darts night, a bit of organising helps. Book the right number of players and arrive a few minutes early. If you've got a big group, split across two oches so everyone gets plenty of throws. Decide who's in charge of picking games, and mix the skill-based formats with the more chaotic ones to keep it fair for beginners.

New to the game? Stand side-on with your leading foot forward, keep your elbow still and throw with a smooth flick of the forearm. Accuracy beats power every time. The tech does all the scoring, so you just need to aim, throw and enjoy the banter with your group. Losers buy the next round of street food at Boxpark, obviously.
